title: Choose Hyperplanner’s visual world
question: Three systems, each built to carry all eight plan palettes. Choose one, steer the hand, or re-roll.

options.label: Pit-Wall Instrument
options.lineage: Formula One pit-wall timing screens and billet data loggers
options.thesis: Every workout reads like a live performance run: the prescription is telemetry, and the next set is the only active command.
options.viewport: A portrait control deck with the target load dominating the upper third, a vertical set ledger below, and a thumb dock carrying the next action.
options.risk: Can feel generically futuristic if the timing hierarchy and physical control details are not carried through every screen.

options.label: Constructed Power Grid
options.thesis: The training prescription is visibly constructed from one rigorous grid, with weights and states becoming the interface’s monumental letterforms.
options.case: Wins audience identification through disciplined strength and keeps product clarity high when the grid remains subordinate to the numbers.
options.viewport: A portrait grid sheet where the current weight occupies a monumental cell field and workouts snap into numbered modules beneath it.
options.risk: The visible grid can become visual noise in dense settings and history screens.

options.label: Industrial Training Issue
options.lineage: industrial streetwear labels, stockroom tags, and hazard grammar
options.thesis: The app behaves like issued training equipment: every zone is plainly labeled, every active command carries the plan’s colored tag, and completion removes it.
options.case: Strongest cultural identification and excellent state clarity; it trades some luxury polish for physical toughness.
options.viewport: A portrait equipment panel with a huge literal workout label, stacked exercise manifests, and one colored tear-tag action in thumb reach.
options.risk: Can read as fashion branding rather than a precision tool if labels outnumber useful training states.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar card-based workout dashboard, executed cleanly and adapted through plan accent tokens.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional workout summary, progress cards, and persistent mobile navigation.
canonCard.risk: Highly usable but least distinctive and easiest to confuse with another fitness product.
